title: POWDER — Riding
description: Board-carving locomotion, air-trick combo scoring, and rideable terrain — the reusable mechanics under an SSX-style snowboarding game.
boundary: Nothing here is wired into engine core. These are reusable RIDING primitives, not POWDER content and not Craftpunk anything. POWDER is the standing second consumer that keeps the engine honest: if a 'primitive' only a snowboarding game could want, it's POWDER data, not a pack entry.

components.name: Board
components.why: Carving state (edge angle, tilt) plus authored ride tunables (grip, sidecut, jump charge). Prototype's tunables.json maps straight onto durable fields here.

components.name: TrickScore
components.why: Air-trick combo state machine — tracks rotation, tick points, multipliers, repeat decay; scores on landing grade. Ports the prototype's trick_scoring.js.

components.name: Terrain
components.why: Rideable surface authored as heightfield / bezier patches (the prototype's patch_course), rendered as a procedural mesh and collided against.
reusableBy: a golf / driving game with contoured ground

types.name: Rider
types.why: A player/agent with a Board + TrickScore, driven by carve locomotion instead of WASD walking.
reusableBy: a vehicle/racing game with a steer+drift model

behaviors.name: carve
behaviors.why: Per-tick board locomotion: slope momentum + edge-grip steering + jump charge/pop. Ports board_physics.js pure functions over durable Board tunables.

behaviors.name: trick
behaviors.why: Detects air, accumulates rotation into named tricks, scores on landing. Ports trick_scoring.js.

substrateGaps.note: Genuine ENGINE (tier-1) gaps POWDER surfaces. Game-agnostic — file as TRLs, not overfit, not a fork. See PORTING.md.
items: Rapier heightfield colliders + continuous-collision (CCD) for fast bodies
Procedural terrain meshes from patch/heightfield data in the render layer
Analog input axes surfaced through the input-map system (stick carving/spin)
